clues: Of the helper in brown mittens and the one who came in at 9:20 p.m., one was Milo and the other Greta.
One of Imani and Greta wore the green mittens, and the other did the inking.
Whoever did the sweeping came in earlier than whoever did the proofing.
Whoever wore the red mittens did either the folding or the bundling.
Imani arrived exactly 40 minutes after Milo.
Selma arrived later than whoever wore the gray mittens.
Quinn came in at either 8:00 p.m. or 8:40 p.m.
Milo did either the inking or the folding.
The helper in green mittens arrived later than Imani.
hints: Look at Imani's row in the time box. Clues 5 and 9 leave just two possible times. Which two?
Time for a Suppose: clue 5 ties Milo to Imani, 40 minutes apart, and clue 7 limits Quinn. Test Imani's earlier time.
Suppose Imani came in at 8:40 p.m. Then clue 5 puts Milo at 8:00, and clue 7 leaves Quinn only 8:00 too, a clash. So Imani came at 9:00.
Greta came in at 9:20, Imani at 9:00 and Milo at 8:20. Clue 6 keeps Selma off 8:00, so Selma came at 8:40.

solution.key_idea: Testing Imani at 8:40 p.m. puts Milo and Quinn both at 8:00, so Imani came at 9:00 and the times fall into place.
steps: By clue 1, Milo or Greta came in at 9:20. Clue 5 puts Milo before Imani, so it was Greta, and Milo wore brown.
Clue 9 keeps Imani out of the green mittens, so by clue 2 Greta wore green and Imani did the inking.
So by clue 8 Milo did the folding, and by clue 4 whoever wore red did the bundling.
Greta, in green, did not bundle, and clue 3 keeps the sweeping off 9:20. So Greta did the proofing.
Clue 5 puts Imani at 8:40 or later, and clue 9 before Greta's 9:20, so at 8:40 or 9:00.
Suppose Imani came in at 8:40. Then clue 5 puts Milo at 8:00, but clue 7 leaves Quinn only 8:00 as well. That cannot be.
So Imani came in at 9:00 and Milo at 8:20. Clue 6 keeps Selma off 8:00, so Selma came at 8:40 and Quinn at 8:00.
Clue 6 puts the gray mittens before Selma: Quinn's. Imani did the inking, so Selma wore red and did the bundling. Quinn swept; Imani wore white.
solution.epilogue: Selma had slipped off a red mitten to knot the twine on a bundle and set it on the press, where the rollers swallowed it. She had been hunting for it ever since.
